reasoning: Both sets are competent plans in the same general shape: one package, a frozen interface task first, then spines, thicken tasks and wiring, with fixture-backed fakes. A has the better content. Its spec, contract and tests are precise, with closed-form golden cases I checked by hand: the Q-update gives 0.1 then 0.009, GAE gives [1.3775, 0.5], swim-vector scaling gives (0.0144, 0.0192), and the compact-view one-hot is correct. It cites its sources (Sutton & Barto, Schulman). It keeps truncation separate from termination and lays out a clear concept ladder for each stage (tabular → DQN → CNN plus ablations; REINFORCE → PPO; fixed opponents → naive co-learning → opponent pool). A's packets carry the types and exact expected values a builder needs. A's weaknesses: three huge milestones, one per stage (M1 has 31 tasks); a contract that freezes fields M1 never uses (self_play, generations); and stale framing (the brief's 'Not doing: designing future environments now', and the S2 outline's 'deliberately revised shared core' against AD-09 'adopted before M1 is built'). B reads more easily for a learner and splits the work into smaller milestones. It also has good ideas: check worlds as a gate before every batch, a REINFORCE spine for PPO, and learner write-ups. But it has real gaps. M1 trains a snake that has no replay buffer, target network or viewer, so the 'watch it' half of the goal is pushed to M2. M3 ('Check and explain the snake': reference check plus write-up) is a leftover milestone. The tests are still Draft with oracles left open: TC-17's bound is 'to be re-derived', yet M1-T25 must pass it, and TC-07's direction is also open. The snake observation gives only the sign of the food offset, but the rule baseline, which is limited to observations, has to move 'along the shorter axis'. The train_loop spine packet leaves out core.Step, WorldSpec, TeamSpec and EpisodeResult. On balance, A's rigour outweighs B's readability.

strengths: Golden cases are exact closed-form oracles with cited sources; spot-checked values are correct
A clear concept ladder per stage (tabular/DQN/CNN plus ablations; REINFORCE/PPO; three self-play rungs with cross-play)
Contract types are code shapes with invariants, errors and fixture cases; truncation and termination kept separate
Library reference mapping is pinned one-to-one, so a gap points at the learner's code
weaknesses: One milestone per stage makes each very large (M1 has 31 tasks)
The M1 contract freezes fields that only S2/S3 need (self_play, pool_latest, generations)
Stale framing in the brief and roadmap about designing future environments and a 'deliberately revised' core
Pipeline step tables list constructors (Snake, DQNAgent, FishTank…) that the entry function never calls

strengths: Readable spec and brief that match the user's out-of-scope list closely
Check worlds with hand-derived answers gate every batch: a good guard against silent RL bugs
Smaller milestones and many small, clear pipelines; replay viewer design with side-by-side and sight overlay
Learner write-ups and a finish check tie directly to 'explain why it works'
weaknesses: M1 delivers no replay and no agent that can beat the baselines; M3 is a leftover reference-check plus write-up milestone
Tests are Draft with unresolved oracles (TC-17 bound, TC-07 direction) that M1 tasks must pass
The snake observation (signs only) can't support the rule baseline's 'shorter axis' choice
The interface task freezes thicken-hook stubs (guard, check_runs, apply_style, holm, verdict), which are private helpers

A: M1-T31: real 5-seed runs for 7+ rungs (ladder, ablations, reference), sized S; the acceptance can be checked but it is far more than one session of wall-clock work
B: M1-T25: acceptance requires TC-17 to pass, but the bound is 'to be re-derived with test-planning', so there is no oracle
M1-T09: the packet omits core.Step, core.WorldSpec/TeamSpec, core.EpisodeResult and guard's signature, yet train_loop must split agents by team and write EpisodeResults
M1-T15: SnakeRule must pick 'the shorter axis' from observations alone, but SNAKE_OBS gives only the sign of food_dx/food_dy
M1-T29: 'passes the dataviz skill's checks' is not a concrete, checkable acceptance criterion
